compiler.methodology: Serial isolated processes. Public production compileLocal. First compile after import reported separately; 2 further warmups and 10 measured calls by default, with per-case/CLI overrides recorded on each result. --once stops after the first compile; --soak replaces timing loops with successive edit versions and GC checkpoints every 10 versions. No forced GC inside ordinary timing loops. Input generation, assertions and optional one-shot structuredClone excluded from compile timing. GC snapshots before/after first compile, with result retained and released. Peak RSS is OS process.resourceUsage maxRSS (KiB converted to bytes), includes runtime/import/input and is captured before correctness traversal or cloning on first compile. Returned node count excludes intermediate allocations. P95 for small sample counts is descriptive only. Uncaught errors, process exits and timeout are separate outcomes. Results written after every case.

blocks.methodology: Serial isolated Node processes per fixture, default V8 heap. Standalone compileLocal plus one target block in the middle of the same 1000 ordinary paragraph background (configurable). Numeric revision has fixed width; fence-delimiter fixture intentionally changes both fence lengths. Three warmups, 21 measured samples by default; long-document full and session calls alternate order. Timer excludes source generation/assertions and includes complete compile result assembly. Formula inspection included; React rendering, syntax highlighting, chart sampling and diagram layout excluded. Block sizes/node counts differ and are reported. P95 uses nearest rank. No cross-machine pass threshold.

parser.methodology: Serial isolated Node processes with --expose-gc and default heap. Version order alternates by case. Timings include complete compileLocal result construction, exclude fixture generation, assertions, hashing and GC. Long-line cases use at most 5 samples and over-budget uses at most 3. Canonical full-result hashes must match. Peak RSS covers the whole child process. Work counters are aggregate parser-call work, measured separately through Vite SSR, not unique source coverage. No rendering.

fast.methodology: Serial child processes, default heap, --expose-gc. Full compile timings exclude source generation/assertions/GC; complete result included. Table cells and list content use a conservative fast subset. Version order alternates per size. SHA256 compares full serialized output of each pair. Retention samples run GC every 20 context edits; recovered result remains alive at disposal. No React rendering.

incremental.methodology: Same production build, one session per case. Appends a changing revision to the last block. Three warmups and fifteen paired measurements in alternating order; default Node heap. Full snapshot assembly is included. Browser rendering and Worker transport excluded.

memory.methodology: Isolated production-package processes with explicit GC before every memory snapshot. Long edits retain the previous preview until its replacement exists. RSS peak covers the entire child; heapUsed is a post-GC snapshot, not total allocations. No hard real-time or cross-machine memory threshold is inferred.

editing.methodology: Production packages built into the same Playwright fixture. Real Edge module Worker, 20ms scheduler delay, react-dom/profiling. Three warmups then fifteen measured textarea edits per scenario; version order alternates by scenario. Median/P95 are descriptive for fifteen samples. Input-to-preview ends at two requestAnimationFrame callbacks after commit, not completed paint. JSON UTF-8 lengths estimate messages, not structured-clone bytes. Before and after are measured sequentially on one machine and are not statistically controlled.

render.methodology: Actual Demo LocalPreview, PreviewStateSession and useLocalCompilation with production packages and react-dom/profiling. React commitRoot/flushMutationEffects/flushLayoutEffects wrapped only in the benchmark build with finally-based wall-clock timing. Each function uses the union of its intervals to avoid counting recursive calls twice; different functions still overlap and must not be summed. Editor render includes preview render. QueueMs is input-to-dispatch, while dispatchWaitMs begins at the scheduling effect. CDP renderer-main-thread Layout, UpdateLayoutTree, PrePaint and Paint event durations per input interval; compositor/GPU completion excluded. First mount recorded separately; two edit warmups and then measured edits. Frame-ready is two requestAnimationFrame callbacks after actual preview DOM mutations, not completed paint. Trace and instrumentation overhead applies to both variants.

stages.methodology: Five warmups per case in headless Chromium against a Vite dev server. compile = compileLocal on a 100-section interactive article (3-curve plot included). update = runtime.set with one no-op subscriber, no React, amortized over 1000 writes. plot = compileLatex + samplePlot for 3 curves x 200 points, amortized over 20 plots. render:final = slider write -> React re-render -> DOM commit -> forced getBoundingClientRect() style/layout on the plot-free 100-section article; its median excludes the runtime write, which is reported separately, and plot sampling is excluded. interaction = the same write on the article version containing the 3-curve plot, so React work includes plot sampling, SVG path generation and DOM updates. locality = one plot-free 100-section article mounted once; three sliders are written in forward and reverse passes (five warmups per pass, samples merged) so drift cancels: a value referenced by every section, a value referenced by exactly one section, and a value referenced by no other node; it isolates how much update cost lies outside the dependency footprint of the written value. visuals = one article made of 10 interpolated tables mounted once; three sliders are written in forward and reverse passes: a value referenced by every table, one referenced by exactly one table, and one referenced by none; it measures how much per-write cost table rendering adds and how much of that cost is independent of the written value. charts = the same footprint comparison on an article made of 4 interpolated bar charts. Paint/presentation after layout is not included. Observations under load, not cross-machine thresholds.
